Job Title:

Senior Director, Enterprise Portfolio Management

Job Description:

The Role:

Entegris is seeking a Senior Director, Enterprise Portfolio Management Office (EPMO) to lead portfolio governance, demand management, and delivery oversight for strategic technology and digital transformation initiatives. 

This leader will partner closely with business and technology executives to ensure investments are aligned to company priorities, appropriately funded and resourced, and delivered in a predictable manner. This leader will establish the processes and governance required to move initiatives efficiently from idea through execution and value realization while driving transparency, accountability, and business outcomes across the portfolio. 

The ideal candidate combines strong portfolio and program leadership experience with the ability to influence executive decision-making, lead organizational change, and improve the effectiveness of enterprise technology investments. 

This position reports directly to the Chief Information & Digital Officer. It will be based local to one of our hubs, ideally in Chaska, MN, Bedford, MA, or Aurora, IL.

 

What You’ll Do:

Enterprise Portfolio Leadership & Governance

Lead the Enterprise Portfolio Management Office (EPMO), establishing portfolio management, governance, and delivery practices that enable successful execution of strategic initiatives.

Oversee enterprise portfolio governance, prioritization, funding, and investment decision-making to ensure alignment with business objectives and organizational capacity.

Serve as a trusted advisor to executive leadership on portfolio strategy, investment priorities, risks, and tradeoffs.

Demand Management & Portfolio Prioritization

Own the enterprise demand management process, providing a transparent framework for evaluating, prioritizing, and approving technology and digital investments.

Lead the end-to-end portfolio lifecycle from intake and business case development through execution and value realization.

Develop portfolio metrics and reporting that provide visibility into demand, capacity, delivery performance, and investment outcomes.

Resource Planning & Portfolio Optimization

Lead enterprise-wide capacity planning and resource forecasting to balance demand, funding, and organizational readiness.

Facilitate executive decision-making regarding investment priorities, resource allocation, and portfolio tradeoffs.

Continuously evaluate portfolio performance and recommend adjustments to maximize business value and delivery effectiveness.

Strategic Program Oversight

Provide executive oversight for large-scale, cross-functional technology and business transformation initiatives.

Ensure effective risk management, governance, financial stewardship, and delivery

Executive Reporting & Value Realization

Provide executive leadership with a consolidated view of portfolio performance, investment health, risks, and realized business value.

Establish value realization measures and drive continuous improvement across portfolio management, governance, and delivery practices.

Organizational Leadership & PMO Maturity

Lead, develop, and inspire a high-performing team of portfolio management professionals.

Build a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement while advancing portfolio management capabilities across the enterprise.

Champion organizational change management and PMO best practices to improve adoption, efficiency, and business outcomes.

What We Seek:

Demonstrated success leading an Enterprise PMO, Portfolio Management Office, or comparable function within a complex global organization.

Extensive experience managing strategic technology portfolios, enterprise transformation initiatives, and portfolio governance processes.

Strong expertise in demand management, prioritization, resource planning, investment management, and value realization.

Deep understanding of portfolio, program, project, Agile, and product delivery methodologies.

Proven ability to influence executive decision-making and build strong partnerships across business and technology functions.

Strong business and financial acumen, including business case development, budgeting, forecasting, and investment planning.

Demonstrated success leading organizational change, improving operating models, and driving measurable business outcomes.

Exceptional communication, stakeholder management, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

Broad understanding of enterprise business processes and supporting technologies across key functional areas.

Outstanding Candidates Will Have:

Master's degree in business administration, Information Systems, Engineering, Computer Science, or related field.

10+ years of progressive leadership experience in portfolio, program, or project management.

Experience leading enterprise portfolios and large-scale digital or business transformation initiatives.

Experience transforming PMO organizations and advancing portfolio management maturity.

Relevant certifications such as PMP, PgMP, PfMP, PMI-ACP, CSM, or equivalent.

Demonstrated track record of delivering measurable business value through technology investments and operational excellence.

Why Work at Entegris? 

Lead. Inspire. Innovate. Define Your Future.

Not everyone who works for a global company shares the same background, experiences and perspectives. We leverage the differences of our employees to bring new ideas to the table. Every employee throughout the company is encouraged to share input on projects and initiatives. Our decision-making process is truly a collaborative effort as we realize there are leaders at every level of the organization. We put our values at the core of how we operate as an organization — not just when it’s convenient, but in a lasting and meaningful way. We want the time and energy you spend here to have a positive impact on your life inside and outside of the office.

What We Offer:

Our total rewards package goes above and beyond just a paycheck. Whether you’re looking to build your career, improve your health, or protect your wealth, we offer generous benefits to help you achieve your goals.

Compensation: $186,500 - $266,500 per year range with actual pay dependent on candidate overall skills for the role

Annual bonus eligibility

Progressive paid time off policy that empowers you to take the time you need to recharge

Generous 401(K) plan with an impressive employer match with no delayed vesting 

Excellent health, dental and vision insurance packages to fit your needs

Education assistance to support your learning journey

A values-driven culture with colleagues that rally around People, Accountability, Creativity and Excellence

Scale Elite Talent: Recruit, mentor, and develop the next wave of Technical and Strategic Builders. Drive technical excellence, structure career growth, and foster an environment where shipping high-quality, production-ready systems is the norm.

Guide Enterprise Implementations: Unblock complex data readiness, tool integration, and multi-agent orchestration challenges. Step in directly to help your teams assess customer technical readiness, remove deployment barriers, and codify standardized, repeatable delivery methodologies.

Drive Agentic Adoption: Build and anchor strong executive-level relationships within your customer portfolio, ensuring flawless Agentforce activation, rollout, and sustained production value.

Accelerate Portfolio Performance: Operationally run your account portfolio with engineering rigor - monitoring health, delivery velocity, and core consumption metrics to accelerate progress toward customer business outcomes.

Cross-Functional Alignment: Partner lock-step with Services, Account Success, and Product teams to help enterprises activate and consume Agentforce quickly, moving customers from pilot to production at hyper-speed.

title: Associate Director - Solutions Portfolio Operations
description:
About Us

Since 1989, SHI International Corp. has helped organizations change the world through technology. We’ve grown every year since, and today we’re proud to be a $16 billion global provider of IT solutions and services.

 

Over 17,000 organizations worldwide rely on SHI’s concierge approach to help them solve what’s next. But the heartbeat of SHI is our employees – all 7,000 of them. If you join our team, you’ll enjoy:

Our commitment to diversity, as the largest minority- and woman-owned enterprise in the U.S.

Continuous professional growth and leadership opportunities.

Health, wellness, and financial benefits to offer peace of mind to you and your family.

World-class facilities and the technology you need to thrive – in our offices or yours. 

Job Summary

We are seeking an Associate Director - Solutions Portfolio Operations to support the evolution of SHI’s portfolio by translating technical capabilities into differentiated, outcome-driven solutions.

Working in close collaboration with Marketing, Sales, Delivery, and other cross-functional teams, this role is responsible for the processes, governance, and operating model SHI uses to bring offerings to market. The Associate Director will oversee solution development, launch, and lifecycle management, helping design customer-centric solutions that align with organizational goals and market demands.

This role will also drive continuous improvement efforts, leveraging new technologies and methodologies to enhance go-to-market effectiveness and enable greater consistency, speed, and quality.

Role Description

Operational Leadership

Lead Solution Marketing portfolio operations, development, and governance.

Translate portfolio strategy into operating plans, resource priorities, decision rights, and measurable outcomes.

Provide leadership visibility into portfolio progress, launches, dependencies, risks, and decisions.

Align Marketing, pillar leaders, technical teams, Services, Sales, Alliances, and Operations around shared portfolio standards and priorities.

Lead adoption of new solution development processes, governance, and tools while balancing enterprise consistency with business needs.

Resolve ownership, priority, and process barriers to keep development and launches moving.

Solution Development Process and Governance

Own and improve SHI’s end-to-end solution development process, from intake and qualification through launch, lifecycle management, and retirement.

Establish consistent requirements for prioritization, approval, documentation, handoffs, and launch readiness.

Partner with technical and business owners to ensure solution inputs are accurate, complete, and market-ready.

Portfolio Operations and Rationalization

Maintain an enterprise-wide view of the solution portfolio across pillars, service lines, partners, and lifecycle stages.

Partner with business and technical leaders to identify gaps, overlap, inconsistent packaging, and opportunities to consolidate or expand offerings.

Organize the portfolio around customer needs and outcomes, including integrated journeys across presales, implementation, optimization, and managed services.

Lead portfolio reviews that inform prioritization, investment, and lifecycle decisions.

Solution Catalog and Content Operations

Govern solution taxonomy, naming, metadata, documentation standards, and catalog readiness.

Ensure approved solution information is consistent across the SHI Solution Catalog, SHI One, marketplaces, co-sell listings, and foundational sales and marketing assets.

Partner with program operations to maintain portfolio accuracy and identify opportunities to automate documentation, publishing, and reporting.

Go-to-Market and Launch Operations

Establish a repeatable launch framework covering positioning, documentation, catalog readiness, sales enablement, communications, partner alignment, and measurement.

Coordinate cross-functional launch plans, owners, dependencies, timing, and success measures.

Ensure effective handoffs from solution development to go-to-market activation and conduct post-launch reviews to improve future execution.

Market, Customer, and Performance Insights

Use customer, market, sales, partner, and performance insights to inform portfolio and solution decisions.

Define and track measures for development cycle time, process adoption, launch readiness, catalog health, seller engagement, solution adoption, and influenced pipeline.

Turn performance findings into recommendations for portfolio, process, and investment improvements.

Behaviors and Competencies

Strategic Thinking: Connect business strategy, customer needs, portfolio decisions, and go-to-market execution.

Operational Leadership: Turn strategy into repeatable processes, clear ownership, and measurable execution.

Portfolio Mindset: Evaluate offerings as an integrated portfolio based on customer value, strategic fit, and business potential.

Business Acumen: Connect portfolio decisions to growth, adoption, customer value, and partner priorities.

Cross-Functional Influence: Align stakeholders and drive decisions across a complex, matrixed organization.

Communication: Simplify complex capabilities, processes, and recommendations for varied audiences.

People Leadership: Build accountable, high-performing teams through clear expectations, coaching, and delegation.

Continuous Improvement: Use data and feedback to improve speed, quality, and scale.

Skill Level Requirements

Solution, service, or product development operating models - Advanced

Portfolio strategy, rationalization, governance, and lifecycle management - Advanced

Cross-functional launch, program, and change management - Advanced

Team leadership and senior stakeholder influence - Advanced

Process design, workflow improvement, and governance - Advanced

Executive communication, facilitation, and business writing - Advanced

Portfolio measurement, dashboards, and reporting - Intermediate to Advanced

B2B technology, IT services, or solution-provider knowledge - Intermediate to Advanced

Other Requirements

Completed bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant work experience required.

8–12 years of experience in solution or product marketing, portfolio or product management, or a related field.

4+ years of experience leading people or complex cross-functional programs.

Demonstrated experience building or improving portfolio, solution development, and launch processes in a B2B technology or services environment.

Ability to travel to SHI, Partner, and Customer Events - up to 25%

The estimated annual pay range for this position is $150,000 - $180,000 which includes a base salary and bonus. The compensation for this position is dependent on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and market location and, therefore, will vary from individual to individual. Benefits may include, but are not limited to, medical, vision, dental, 401K, and flexible spending

Equal Employment Opportunity – M/F/Disability/Protected Veteran Status

description:
Are you an experienced Statistical Programming professional with deep knowledge of clinical drug development? Would you like to use your technical expertise to provide strategic programming leadership and help shape the delivery of clinical development programmes? Join us at AstraZeneca CVRM (Cardiovascular Renal Metabolism) Biometrics to impact a wide range of engaging projects striving to make a difference for millions of patients. Our Biometrics team consists of Statisticians, Programmers, Information and Data Scientists. We drive and contribute to optimized clinical drug development programs and access to information and scientific knowledge management.

We are now offering an exciting opportunity for a dedicated and highly motivated individual to join us as Statistical Programming, Associate Director, providing strategic programming leadership within CVRM Biometrics and collaborating with global product development teams.

This role is primarily focused on strategic and technical leadership, planning and project management rather than hands-on statistical programming. You will draw on your technical programming expertise to provide direction, oversee delivery and support high-quality decision-making.

This role will be placed at AstraZeneca’s dynamic R&D strategic site in Gothenburg (Sweden), where you will work in an international environment at the forefront of clinical development.

Accountabilities:

As a Statistical Programming, Associate Director, you are accountable for quality, timely and efficient delivery of project programming work and information management. This position requires profound programming experience and excellent industry knowledge to provide strategic and technical leadership across programming activities, including planning and project management. This is a strategic leadership role with project and technical focus where you will provide subject matter expertise within the statistical programming discipline. You will oversee the delivery of data according to industry standards, and high-quality statistical analyses and reporting deliverables, as well as planning and execution of submission strategies. You will act as a specialist within cross-functional teams to drive continuous improvement, innovation, and automation solutions.

Essential Skills/Experience:

Degree in Mathematics (e.g., Applied Math, Engineering, etc.), Statistics, Computer Science, Life Science, or equivalent experience

Advanced knowledge of the clinical development process and industry standards

Demonstrated programming leadership capability, with the ability to provide strategic and technical direction, develop teams and individuals, and lead them towards a common goal without formal line management responsibility

Demonstrated influencing, planning and organizational skills

Ability to provide input to functional strategies

Expertise in risk management in complex or novel situations

Strong technical experience in SAS and CDISC standards, together with current knowledge and awareness of regulatory requirements relevant to Statistical Programming

 

Desirable Skills/Experience:

Broad experience, ideally across multiple therapeutic areas and/or beyond Statistical Programming

Experience in regulatory submissions and regulatory interactions

Demonstrated experience in designing and implementing business processes

Willingness and ability to travel

At AstraZeneca, we believe in the potential of our people, and you’ll develop beyond what you thought possible. We make the most of your skills and passion by actively supporting you to see what you can achieve no matter where you start with us. In this role, you’ll play a pivotal role in channeling our scientific capabilities to make a positive impact on changing patients’ lives and join us on an exciting journey to pioneer the future of healthcare.

This role is an office-based role with some degree of flexibility. Our vibrant office sites provide a diverse and collaborative work environment, where interactions lead to ideas and innovations, giving you and others the perfect opportunity to learn, grow and develop careers.

Are you ready to bring new ideas and fresh thinking to the table? Brilliant! We have a seat available, and we hope it’s yours. Apply today!

Welcome with your application no later than November 18th, 2026.

title: Director EUIT, Finance Product Impact, Value and Portfolio
description:
The Director, Finance Product Impact, Value and Portfolio is accountable for proving and growing the value delivered by all 17 Finance IT products across Core Finance and Finance Planning and Analytics. This role owns product health and maturity measurement, value-realisation and benefits tracking against the run-cost bridge, the product portfolio and demand pipeline, product craft standards, and the single in-house performance scorecard for AI agents and partner delivery pods. Reporting to the Executive Director, Finance IT, and leading a team of four, the Director gives the leadership team the evidence needed to decide where to invest, sustain, consolidate or retire, and to confirm that the product-and-platform operating model is delivering outcomes, not just activity. Central to the role is making the true value of IT visible and credible to the business; recognising IT not merely as a cost to be contained but as a driver of capacity, speed, quality, control and competitive advantage for the Core Functions and translating that value into hard outcomes, including a measurable productivity saving of at least 10% for each function served. The Director partners closely with the two Product Line Leads, the Senior Director Product Design and Solutions, the Director Transformation and Product Experience, senior Finance business leaders, strategic partners, Procurement, and Central Technology Risk and Data Governance to maximise value and innovation in a product-centric organisation. 

  

Key Responsibilities  

Value Realisation and Benefits Tracking: Define and run the value-measurement discipline across all 17 products, tracking benefits against the run-cost bridge ($20.0M today to the $15.0M plan of record and the $13.5M stretch aim). Report the value of agents that run IT itself and of agents that serve the business separately, never netted. Own the target of delivering a 10% productivity saving for each Core Function releasing time, effort and spend to be reinvested in higher-value work and evidence it product by product alongside the run-cost bridge, so the function sees a clear, auditable return on its IT investment.  

• Product Health and Maturity: Maintain one consistent health and maturity view of every product, covering adoption, quality, user experience, run cost and control health. Trigger intervention with the Product Line Leads where a product falls below threshold, and keep the evidence base current for leadership and gate reviews.  

• Portfolio and Demand Management: Own the portfolio and demand pipeline and keep prioritisation honest. Recommend which products to invest in, sustain, consolidate or retire, and support the phased launch of the 17 products.  

• Agent and Pod Performance Scorecard: Own the single scorecard for AI agents and partner delivery pods, covering accuracy, deflection, Service-Level Agreement and Experience-Level Agreement performance, and cost. Provide the evidence for the agent governance plane and for the two-of-four pause criterion at each phase gate.  

• Product Craft and Standards: Raise product-management craft across Product Owners and Product Analysts through standards, playbooks, coaching and a graduate pipeline, so that every product team operates to a consistent, defensible bar.  

• Team Leadership: Lead and develop a high-performing team of four, comprising two Value Measurement Leads and two Product Craft and Agent Scorecard specialists. Foster a culture of evidence, accountability and continuous improvement, and own talent development and succession planning for key roles.  

• Stakeholder and Partner Management: Manage and influence the Executive Director, Product Line Leads and senior Finance business leaders on value and portfolio decisions. Hold the embedded Outsourcing partner to account on outcome measures, working with EUIT Operational Excellence on supplier governance and with Procurement on commercial terms such as gain-share and service credits.  

• Governance, Risk and Compliance: Ensure value, benefits and scorecard reporting is auditable and evidence-based. Work with Central Technology Risk and Data Governance on AI guardrails, and ensure no agent is treated as a control until the first clean financial year-end and per-agent auditor sign-off are in place. 

• AI Adoption and Change Management: Be the thought leader for measuring the impact of AI digital workers. Feed adoption and performance evidence to the Director Transformation and Product Experience and the Senior Director Product Design and Solutions so that digital-worker leverage is directed where it creates most value. 

• Budget Management: Develop, deliver and monitor the budget, including capital, for the Product Impact, Value and Portfolio area, and track the savings run-rate against plan, flagging early where it falls below 85% of plan.  

Key Qualifications, Skills and Experience  

Key Qualifications:  

• Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field of study – Finance, Business, Engineering, Computer Science or Information Technology. Masters degree desirable.  

• Significant experience in a client-facing IT or product role, including strategic planning, business plan and case development, and client management.  

• Significant experience in value realisation and benefits tracking, including business models, operating models, financial models, cost-benefit analysis, budgeting and risk management.  

• Significant experience in product-centric operating models, including product portfolio and demand management, product health and maturity measurement, and product-management craft.  

• Significant experience working with diverse business ecosystems, Cloud and software-as-a-service models, and business applications. More specifically: SAP S/4HANA, BlackLine, Anaplan, Snowflake, Coupa, Concur and AWS Bedrock plus AI foundation models, large language models and measuring the performance of AI agents.  

• Significant experience in one or more Finance areas with a comprehensive understanding of business processes and drivers for success, such as record to report, purchase to pay, order to cash, and planning and forecasting.  

• Experience working with regulatory and control aspects of IT solutions in Finance, including Sarbanes-Oxley attestation and audit-ready evidence.  

• Experience having led large-scale change initiatives from planning to implementation.  

• Experience managing teams with direct and indirect reports, including work delivered through outsourced managed-service partners.  

• Experience managing outcome-based managed-service contracts, including Service-Level Agreements, Experience-Level Agreements, service credits and gain-share mechanisms.  

• Experience in co-working with cross-functional global leadership and other senior stakeholders preferred.  

• Substantial experience managing in a global matrix organisation with geographically dispersed teams.  

• Substantial experience communicating with and influencing diverse internal and external stakeholders, including supplier and vendor networks, across areas and geographies to drive value and portfolio outcomes.  

• Substantial experience anticipating, assessing and managing programme and portfolio risks.  

• Certification in product management, portfolio management or business analysis preferred.  

  

Skills & Technical Proficiency:  

• Critical/ Strategic Thinking: Influences the broader business strategy with data and insights and anticipates futuristic changes.  

• Results & Execution Focus: Sets ambitious yet realistic value targets, measures them rigorously and holds product teams and partners to outcomes.  

• Business & Sustainability: Leverages a strong understanding of the organisational structure and business financials to make strategic recommendations and advocate for sustainable business strategies.  

• Adaptability & Change Orientation: Champions bold moves and systemic changes and models resilience when faced with unexpected changes.  

• Communication, Collaboration & Influence: Is an inspiring communicator, builds strong partnerships, and bridges silos to achieve broader organisational goals.  

• Talent Development: Champions a culture based on feedforward, coaching, and stretch development and ensures a level playing field for diverse talent.  

• Business & Customer Centricity: Leverages a strong understanding of Finance functional domains, customer processes and the related IT landscape to judge where product investment creates most value.  

• Value & Insight Storytelling: Turns product, cost and performance data into clear, decision-ready evidence for the Executive Director and senior Finance leaders, and is candid when the evidence is unwelcome.  

• Product Craft & Portfolio Judgement: Applies product-management standards and portfolio thinking to prioritise, sequence and retire products, balancing value, risk and capacity.  

• AI Performance Measurement: Designs and runs measures for AI agents and partner delivery pods, and drives a culture of proactive change, skill building and application around emerging technologies and ways of working. 

Next Steps?

title: Principal Software Architect
description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Product Architecture and Safety Teams

Our Product Architecture and Safety teams connect Wayve’s core AI Driver with the vehicle platforms that bring autonomous driving technology to customers. Working across Engineering, Product, Safety, Validation and customer programs, we define how our software integrates with OEM and Tier 1 systems, supporting safe, reliable deployment while maintaining a consistent core product architecture.

🧠 Your day-to-day

As a Principal Software Architect, you’ll lead the technical architecture for integrating Wayve’s autonomous driving technology with automotive OEM vehicle platforms. You’ll work at the boundary between our core AI Driver and external vehicle systems, translating product ambitions and customer needs into clear interfaces, requirements and technical decisions.

Your work will span high-level architecture and implementation details, from sensors and middleware to ECU constraints, timing, diagnostics, safety assumptions, data logging and validation. You’ll bring structure to ambiguous problems, guide architecture work across teams and own key decisions across customer programs. Along the way, you’ll build alignment with engineering, product, safety, validation, program and commercial leaders.

🧩 What you’ll be working on

  • Defining integration architecture: Shape how Wayve software interfaces with OEM and Tier 1 vehicle systems, balancing customer program needs with the evolution and reusability of our core architecture.

  • Making ownership explicit: Turn customer and partner discussions into clear interface contracts, ownership boundaries, assumptions, dependencies and open technical decisions, including what is Wayve-owned, partner-owned, jointly defined or out of scope.

  • Translating needs into requirements: Partner with Product and Engineering to develop actionable technical specifications. Establish a consistent approach to decomposing customer requirements into system and software requirements, including allocation, traceability and change control.

  • Owning architecture decisions: Lead architecture reviews, maintain decision records and make the final technical call within your scope when consensus cannot be reached.

  • Planning for successful delivery: Assess feasibility, integration complexity, technical gaps and risks. Identify dependencies and required partner deliverables to support customer program planning.

  • Building verifiable solutions: Work with Safety and Validation teams to define safety assumptions, integration test requirements and clear evidence that customer requirements have been met.

  • Representing Wayve with partners: Lead technical discussions with OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers, supported by clear interface specifications, integration guides, architecture diagrams and decision records.

  • Leading across teams: Coordinate architects and engineering teams, negotiate competing priorities, resolve or escalate conflicts early, and mentor architects and senior engineers to build a shared architecture culture.

🙌 You should apply if

  • You bring substantial experience in ADAS, autonomous driving, embedded software or vehicle systems, particularly at the software–vehicle interface. Typically, you’ll have 12+ years of relevant experience, including architecture ownership for a complete product or multiple programs.

  • You can define clear product boundaries, ownership models and interface contracts between internal software and external vehicle systems.

  • You understand vehicle electronics and embedded software constraints, including ECU integration, real-time execution, timing, diagnostics and production vehicle software environments.

  • You’re familiar with automotive communication protocols and electrical/electronic architectures, such as CAN, FlexRay, Automotive Ethernet, SOME/IP or AUTOSAR.

  • You’ve worked with automotive OEMs or Tier 1 suppliers and can navigate their requirements, standards and integration constraints.

  • You’ve established and run requirements processes across multiple teams or programs, translating ambiguous needs into clear, traceable and verifiable system and software specifications.

  • You can move confidently between system-level architecture and implementation details, making sound technical decisions under uncertainty and maintaining consistency as programs evolve.

  • You’ve led architecture work across teams and influenced senior stakeholders without direct authority, building support and handling competing priorities constructively.

  • You communicate complex technical ideas clearly through specifications, diagrams and reviews, and enjoy mentoring others.

 

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

 

More about Wayve:

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

 

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

 

🔍 The Interview Process:

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

  • Initial call / recruiter screen

  • Hiring Manager Interview

  • Deep-dive technical interviews

  • Final interview: mission & values alignment

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

What’s in it for you (Location dependant):

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually
📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve
✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable
✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs
📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth
🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

For more information visit Careers at Wayve. To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve

DISCLAIMER: We will not ask about marriage or pregnancy, care responsibilities or disabilities in any of our job adverts or interviews. However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory.

title: Director, Regulatory Compliance UK
description:
About Airwallex

Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full.

 

About the Role

We hire builders with founder-level energy—people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do.

As Director, Regulatory Compliance (UK), you will serve as the senior compliance authority and strategic partner for Airwallex’s rapidly expanding UK presence. Operating as a licensed Electronic Money Institution (EMI) supervised by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), Airwallex requires compliance leadership that sees regulatory integrity not as a roadblock, but as a critical commercial enabler and competitive differentiator.

In this role, you will lead our UK compliance framework, serve as the primary interface with local regulators and industry bodies, and work cross-functionally across Product, Strategy, Commercial, and Operations to safely launch cutting-edge payment infrastructure.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead UK Regulatory Compliance: Lead a UK-based team of regulatory compliance professionals; own and continuously evolve the UK compliance management system, policies, registers, and operational controls to ensure ongoing compliance with FCA handbooks, PSRs, EMRs, and UK AML/CTF regimes.

  • Drive FCA Engagement: Act as the principal point of contact for the FCA, handling regulatory inquiries, notifications, audits, thematic reviews, and routine reporting with transparency and authority.

  • Product & Commercial Advisory: Partner early with Product, Commercial, and International Expansion teams to design compliant-by-default cross-border payment, issuing, acquiring, and embedded finance architectures.

  • Safeguarding & Governance: Oversee compliance aspects of key UK regulatory regimes including safeguardingand Consumer Duty in close partnership with Finance, Risk, Product, and other teams.

  • Regulatory Horizon Scanning: Monitor domestic and international regulatory developments (e.g., Consumer Duty, operational resilience, PSR APP fraud reimbursement schemes) and proactively translate emerging rules into pragmatic technical and operational roadmaps.

  • Team Leadership & Culture: Build, coach, and scale a high-caliber UK compliance advisory and operations team while fostering a company-wide culture of risk accountability and ethical rigor.

  • Board & Committee Reporting: Prepare and deliver clear, actionable regulatory compliance reporting and key risk indicator (KRI) updates to executive leadership, local operating boards, and audit/risk committees.

What We’re Looking For

Essentials

  • 10+ years of regulatory compliance experience within UK fintech, payment services (EMIs/APIs), neo-banking, or modern global financial institutions.

  • Leadership Track Record: At least 4+ years managing and developing high-performing compliance teams in high-growth environments.

  • Deep Regulatory Knowledge: Expert grasp of UK financial regulations, including the Payment Services Regulations (PSRs), Electronic Money Regulations (EMRs), FCA Principles for Businesses, and Consumer Duty standards.

  • FCA Interface Experience: Direct track record of managing formal regulator relationships, supervisory inspections, or key authorization filings with the FCA.

  • Pragmatic Problem-Solving: Ability to interpret complex regulatory requirements through a first-principles lens, providing creative, commercial, and defensible paths forward.

  • Executive Presence: Strong communication, negotiation, and written advocacy skills capable of influencing board members, executive partners, and external regulatory bodies.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Prior experience holding an approved person / Senior Management Function (SMF) role under the FCA regime.

  • Background handling regulatory aspects of cross-border multi-currency schemes, merchant acquiring, or credit/lending adjacencies.

  • Relevant legal qualification or industry certifications (e.g., ICA Diploma in Governance, Risk & Compliance).

You’ll Thrive Here If

  • You own the outcome: You don't wait for permission to solve structural bottlenecks—give you a complex regulatory challenge, and you chart the solution.

  • You’re commercially astute: You understand that compliance is an enabler of sustainable hyper-growth, not an isolated checklist.

  • You balance technical precision with plain-English clarity: You can dissect statutory instruments line by line, then distill the essence clearly for engineers, sales leads, and executives.

  • You’re not precious about traditional playbooks: You push hard from first principles, challenging legacy banking compliance norms with modernized, technology-driven solutions.

  • You value in-person collaboration: You thrive working shoulder-to-shoulder with cross-functional leaders in our London hub.

What Success Looks Like

  • Within 3 Months: Complete a comprehensive assessment of our existing UK compliance controls, policies, and FCA commitments; build alignment with key UK commercial leads and partner banks.

  • Within 6 Months: Streamline product approval compliance workflows; enhance local risk governance reporting; and lead strategic readiness for any pending UK regulatory changes.

  • Within 12 Months: Institutionalize a top-tier UK compliance function that scales seamlessly with transaction volume and new market offerings while maintaining an immaculate standing with the FCA.

Why Join Airwallex

  • Competitive base salary, performance incentives, and meaningful equity.

  • High autonomy to build, scale, and influence the core infrastructure powering the global digital economy.

  • Comprehensive health, wellness, pension, and parental leave coverage.

  • Dynamic, global culture with clear paths for rapid professional development.

Equal Opportunity

Airwallex is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and evaluate candidates based on merit, competence, and talent, without regard to race, religion, gender, sexual orientation, disability, or veteran status.

Applicant Safety Policy: Fraud and Third-Party Recruiters

To protect you from recruitment scams, please be aware that Airwallex will not ask for bank details, sensitive ID numbers (i.e. passport), or any form of payment during the application or interview process. All official communication will come from an @airwallex.com email address. Please apply only through careers.airwallex.com or our official LinkedIn page.

Airwallex does not accept unsolicited resumes from search firms/recruiters. Airwallex will not pay any fees to search firms/recruiters if a candidate is submitted by a search firm/recruiter unless an agreement has been entered into with respect to specific open position(s). Search firms/recruiters submitting resumes to Airwallex on an unsolicited basis shall be deemed to accept this condition, regardless of any other provision to the contrary.

Equal opportunity

Airwallex is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and anyone seeking employment at Airwallex is considered based on merit, qualifications, competence and talent. We don’t regard color, religion, race, national origin, sexual orientation, ancestry, citizenship, sex, marital or family status, disability, gender, or any other legally protected status when making our hiring decisions. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

  • Lead our enterprise prospects’ journeys from consideration to successful deployment.

  • Partner with solutions and research engineering to build and execute complex customer programs and projects.

  • Analyse key account metrics to create reports and provide insights to internal and external stakeholders.

  • Support the recruitment and onboarding of other teammates.

  • Support the development of company culture.

title: Senior Accessibility Program Manager
description:
About GitHub

GitHub is the world’s leading platform for agentic software development — powered by Copilot to build, scale, and deliver secure software. Over 180 million developers, including more than 90% of the Fortune 100 companies, use GitHub to collaborate, and more than 77,000 organisations have adopted GitHub Copilot.

Locations

In this role you can work from Remote, United States

Overview

At GitHub, our mission is to accelerate human progress through developer collaboration. We believe people with disabilities should benefit from that progress and directly contribute to the creation of it. 

 

We are seeking a forward-thinking, determined and innovative individual, who is passionate about the intersection of accessibility and technology, to help implement our accessibility strategy, which can be found at accessibility.github.com. This role will report directly to the Head of Accessibility and will be empowered to drive change internally and externally. 

 

 The successful candidate will:

  • Have a deep understanding of accessibility, assistive technologies, and the ways that people with disabilities interact with technology.
  • Have technical expertise that is grounded in professional experience as a software developer or designer.
  • Have hands-on experience using AI and automation to improve accessibility at scale.
  • Have professional experience managing accessibility initiatives within a large matrixed organization.
  • Have a proven track record of delivering results that empower people with disabilities to use technology. 

Responsibilities

 The goals of the GitHub accessibility program are to: 

  • Empower GitHub employees to do the best work of their lives by creating an accessible work environment with internal guides and support for procurement processes.

  • Empower developers with disabilities to build on GitHub by including their input throughout the development process, cultivating a culture of accessibility within GitHub, and driving accountability at scale.

  • Empower our customers to meet their accessibility goals when building on GitHub by aggressively dogfooding the latest GitHub platform and AI features to run our internal accessibility program, Open-sourcing our internal tools when appropriate, and sharing best practices externally.

  • Help improve the accessibility of open source by empowering people with disabilities to contribute, improving the availability and adoption of open-source Assistive Technologies, and improving the accessibility of mainstream open-source projects. 

The Senior Accessibility Program Manager may contribute to all of those program goals over time. That said, their initial focus will include, but is not limited to:

  • Manage listening systems including inclusive user research and feedback processes.
  • Build an accessibility community of practice within our Enterprise customer community.
  • Grow the capabilities of the open-source GitHub accessibility scanner and accelerate adoption by customers and open-source communities. 

Qualifications

Required Qualifications :

  • 7+ years experience in Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), sustainability, accessibility engineering and design, or related area 

    • OR Bachelor's Degree in Business, Sustainability, Computer Science, Communications/Marketing, or related field AND 5+ years experience in Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), sustainability, accessibility engineering and design, or related area 

    • OR Master's Degree in Business, Sustainability, Computer Science, Communications/Marketing, or related field AND 3+ years experience in Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), sustainability, accessibility engineering and design, or related area

    • OR Doctorate in Business, Sustainability, Computer Science, Communications/Marketing, or related field AND 1+ year(s) experience in Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), sustainability, accessibility engineering and design, or related area

    • OR equivalent experience

  • 3+ years of relevant experience driving programs or initiatives across organizational boundaries in a large organization.
  • 3+ years of experience evaluating the conformance of web content against the Web Content Accessibility guidelines.
  • 1+ years of hands-on experience using AI and automation to improve accessibility at scale. 

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience developing accessible web-based user interfaces using JavaScript and modern web technologies.
  • Experience collecting and interpreting data for performance metrics and compliance.
  • Understanding of product road mapping and experience working with product and engineering teams to embed new features into roadmap plans. 

We encourage people with lived experience to apply. 


Compensation Range

The base salary range for this job is USD $103,200.00 - USD $273,700.00 /Yr.

These pay ranges are intended to cover roles based across the United States. An individual's base pay depends on various factors including geographical location and review of experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant. At GitHub certain roles are eligible for benefits and additional rewards, including annual bonus and stock. These rewards are allocated based on individual impact in role. In addition, certain roles also have the opportunity to earn sales incentives based on revenue or utilization, depending on the terms of the plan and the employee's role.

description:
About GitHub

GitHub is the world’s leading platform for agentic software development — powered by Copilot to build, scale, and deliver secure software. Over 180 million developers, including more than 90% of the Fortune 100 companies, use GitHub to collaborate, and more than 77,000 organisations have adopted GitHub Copilot.

Locations

In this role you can work from Remote, United States

Overview

GitHub is seeking a detail-oriented individual contributor with a technical bent and experience in technical risk management who is driven to deepen that expertise. GitHub is committed to doing right by our customers and developing a highly effective control environment where risk is managed in a meaningful and sensible way that aligns with our business. 

  • Do you love the challenge of diving into the details and learning why and how things work? 

  • Do you find yourself always asking what would have to go wrong, and how badly? 

  • Do you want to see The Big Picture, and find ways to collect and organize data to tell the story? 

  • Do you suffer from a compulsive need to document things and “get it down on paper”? 

  • And last, but most certainly not least, have you already answered the question “Why are we here?” with the GRC Truth, “Because Customers”? 

 

If so, you might be the person we are looking for! 

 

As part of GRC’s Entity Risk function, you will join the Technical Risk team and partner with engineering, security, and product subject-matter experts and leaders across GitHub to conduct capability risk assessments, develop and quantify risk scenarios, and deliver meaningful risk reporting that helps leaders make risk-informed decisions. 

Central to the team's culture is that of inclusion, transparency, and teamwork - we lift each other up to be successful! This is an excellent opportunity for an independent contributor to have a hand in elevating risk management and security as business and sales enabler as well as integrate a deeper understanding of risk management into the product and business space. 


Responsibilities

  • Lead security capability risk assessments for assigned areas, including scoping against NIST CSF subcategories, coordinating schedules and stakeholder interviews, completing maturity scoring, and publishing assessment reports. 

  • Analyze data from multiple sources to identify, analyze, and prioritize technical risks, develop and quantify FAIR-style cyber risk scenarios, evaluate capabilities against established frameworks, and assess potential impacts to GitHub – our products, services, customers, and business objectives. 

  • Partner with engineering, security, and product subject-matter experts and leaders to validate findings, identify risk patterns, and translate technical insights and stakeholder feedback into practical risk recommendations. 

  • Develop and manage risk treatment plans, drive adoption of appropriate mitigations and remediation, monitor treatment progress, and escalate unresolved or emerging risks. 

  • Maintain the risk register and supporting records in GitHub’s GRC system of record, track mitigation progress, and provide clear, recurring risk updates to technical and non-technical leaders. 

 


Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

  • 7+ years experience in security analysis, security research, cyber security, security engineering, software engineering, or relevant area; 

    • o OR Associate's Degree AND 6+ years experience in security analysis, security research, cyber security, security engineering, software engineering, or relevant area
    • o OR Bachelor's Degree AND 5+ years experience in security analysis, security research, cyber security, security engineering, software engineering, or relevant area
    • o OR Master's Degree AND 3+ years experience in security analysis, security research, cyber security, security engineering, software engineering, or relevant area
    • o OR Doctorate AND 1+ year(s) experience in security analysis, security research, cyber security, security engineering, software engineering, or relevant area
    • o OR equivalent experience.

  • 5+ years experience applying security or control frameworks, such as NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-53, or ISO/IEC 27001. 

  • 5+ years experience in technical risk management, information security, audit, or compliance. 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience applying cyber risk quantification (CRQ) using FAIR or a comparable quantitative risk analysis method, including developing risk scenarios and estimating loss event frequency and loss magnitude to produce defensible loss exposure ranges that express risk in financial terms and support risk-informed investment and risk-acceptance decisions.  

  • Experience with GRC platforms used to maintain risk registers and risk treatment plans (ZenGRC, ServiceNow GRC, Archer, or comparable). 

  • Experience building risk reporting, metrics, or automation using Azure Data Explorer (Kusto/KQL), Excel, Google Sheets, SQL, Python, or comparable tools. 

  • Experience translating security and compliance requirements between business stakeholders and technical engineering or operations teams. 

  • CISSP, CRISC, CISA, Open FAIR, or a comparable independent certification.

Description

Amazon Robotics is seeking a talented and motivated Senior Technical Program Manager to lead hardware program delivery for the Sortation Vertical. You will own the full program lifecycle for next-generation sortation hardware — from concept through engineering validation, multi-site deployment, and sustaining support in the field.

Are you inspired by invention? Is problem solving through teamwork in your DNA? Do you like the

idea of seeing how your work impacts the bigger picture? Answer yes to any of these and you'll fit

right in here at Amazon Robotics. We are a smart team of doers that work passionately to apply

advances in robotics and software to solve real-world challenges that will transform our customers'

experiences in ways we can't even imagine yet.

This role sits on the Sortation Hardware Engineering team and is the single-threaded program owner for our hardware portfolio. You will drive the mechanical and electromechanical programs that deploy into Amazon's Sortation Centers at scale, working across Systems Engineering, Deployment Engineering, Solutions, Manufacturing and Supply Chain, Product, and Customer Support. You will own the program schedule, the change-control cadence, the supplier and procurement path, and the launch readiness gate — and you will be accountable when those slip.

You will be successful in this role if you are equally comfortable running a design review, chasing

a long-lead component through a contract manufacturer, and standing on a sort center floor at 6am during an install.

Key job responsibilities

• You will own end-to-end delivery of sortation hardware programs across all engineering disciplines, holding the schedule and the critical path across teams that do not report to you and driving technical decisions to closure on the record. 

• You will own the change-control cadence for the hardware portfolio, ensuring our contract manufacturers and deployment partners build to the released revision.

• You will own the procurement path for program hardware, translating supplier lead times on long-lead components into schedule risk before they become launch impacts. 

• You will own launch readiness for site deployments through the go/no-go decision and the handover to site Reliability Maintenance Engineering and Operations, and you will sustain solutions already in the field.

A day in the life

One morning you are deciding whether a bracket that does not fit stops a live install. That afternoon you are working out whether a cable assembly running three weeks late moves a launch date, and pushing a stalled engineering change through to release. Some weeks you are at your desk owning the schedule and the readiness summary leadership will read before a site goes live. Some weeks you are on a sort center floor with a tape measure. Both are the job.

Basic Qualifications

- 5+ years of technical program management experience

- Experience managing programs across cross-functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules

- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Manufacturing, or Industrial Engineering, or a related technical field

- 5+ years of experience working directly with hardware engineering teams

- Experience taking electromechanical hardware from prototype through production and field deployment

Preferred Qualifications

- 7+ years of technical program management experience

- Experience designing or implementing integrated automation solutions such as material handling systems, high-speed packaging lines, or manufacturing lines

- 4+ years of change management experience

- Experience managing contract manufacturers and long-lead component supply chains, including translating lead-time risk into schedule impact

- Experience managing NPI validation gates (EVT/DVT/PVT) and multi-site deployment launches

- Experience with capital planning and procurement mechanics — purchase requisitions, capital requests, and vendor qualification

- Experience owning technology handover to a maintenance or operations organization

- Master's degree, MBA, or PMP certification

Over 180 million developers, including more than 90% of the Fortune 100 companies, use GitHub to collaborate, and more than 77,000 organisations have adopted GitHub Copilot.

Locations

In this role you can work from Remote, United States

Overview

GitHub is looking for a GTM Enablement Specialist to translate important business, product, market, and go-to-market priorities into clear, actionable enablement for our global Revenue organization. 

 

This role will support and own enablement programs across a dynamic portfolio of strategic priorities and business moments. The GTM Enablement Specialist will flex across evolving priorities based on where enablement can create the greatest impact. 

 

You will partner across Revenue, Product Marketing, Product, Revenue Operations, and other teams to understand business and field needs, recommend effective enablement approaches, and build scalable programs that support adoption, behavior change, and strong field execution. 


Responsibilities

  • Collaboratively own the planning, development, execution, and continuous improvement of enablement for assigned GTM initiatives and business moments. 

  • Partner with stakeholders and customer-facing teams to understand business needs, field challenges, capability gaps, and barriers to execution. 

  • Translate complex product, market, competitive, and business changes into clear, actionable guidance for customer-facing teams. 

  • Design scalable enablement experiences using the right mix of live, asynchronous, manager-led, and self-service approaches. 

  • Develop field-facing resources such as enablement sessions, playbooks, job aids, talk tracks, competitive guidance, and manager resources. 

  • Apply change-management principles and reinforcement strategies to support adoption and sustained behavior change. 

  • Manage cross-functional contributors, timelines, dependencies, risks, and deliverables from initial planning through field activation. 

  • Use field feedback, engagement data, adoption signals, and relevant business insights to evaluate effectiveness and continuously improve programs. 

  • Apply AI and emerging technologies to improve the speed, scale, personalization, and effectiveness of enablement. 


Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • 3+ years experience in Sales, Customer Success, Product Management, Consulting, Enablement, Change Management, or related field 

o OR Bachelor's Degree in Business, Marketing, Communications, Operations, Finance or related field AND 1+ year(s) experience in Sales, Customer Success, Product Management, Consulting, Enablement, Change Management, or related field

o OR equivalent experience. 

  • 2+ years experience in program management with the ability to manage competing priorities, dependencies, and deadlines, including owning cross-functional programs from planning through execution and evaluation.
  • 2+ years experience using qualitative and quantitative insights to evaluate effectiveness and inform improvements. 
  • Experience preparing and delivering presentations, producing clear written communications, and facilitating meetings or discussions that drive alignment and decisions.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Demonstrated ability to simplify complex product, market, competitive, or business concepts for customer-facing audiences. 
  • 2+ years experience independently owning cross-functional programs from planning through execution and evaluation. 
  • Ability to understand business and field needs and translate them into practical, scalable solutions. 
  • Experience supporting complex launches, GTM motions, strategic initiatives, or field transformation. 
  • Experience using AI to improve enablement development, delivery, measurement, or field productivity. 
  • Experience in a global SaaS, cloud, AI, developer tools, or enterprise technology organization.

title: Senior TPM, Mathematical Software & Algorithms
description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 
ABOUT THE JOB
 
The Technical Program Manager, Mathematical Software and Algorithms is responsible for overseeing the development, execution, and delivery of the Battlespace Awareness software for critical programs - ensuring it meets all technical, functional, and business requirements. Battlespace Awareness software services comprise advanced algorithms for sense-making and decision-making at tactical timelines.  This role requires an individual with a strong technical background in software development, particularly in the domain of optimization and estimation, and experience managing complex projects with multiple sub-teams and many stakeholders. The Sr Technical Program Manager will be the linchpin in ensuring that the software is developed in line with the objectives defined and is released according to the planned schedule.
 
WHAT YOU'LL DO
  • Project Leadership and Strategy:
    • Develop and maintain a detailed project and execution plan - including feature development, testing and validation, deployment, and monitoring. 
    • Establish clear objectives and deliverables for the software that align with program needs.
  • Technical Expertise:
    • Maintain a deep understanding of underlying algorithms and software interfaces for battle management, threat prediction, tracking, and classification to ensure that the relevant services integrate effectively with the larger C2 system.
    • Stay updated on the latest techniques to work with subject matter experts in incorporating relevant innovations into the project plan.
  • Documentation and Process Improvement:
    • Ensure comprehensive documentation is maintained for the project, including technical specifications, user manuals, and project reports.
    • Continuously evaluate and improve project management processes to increase efficiency and effectiveness.
  • Release Management:
    • Oversee the planning and execution of the software release process, ensuring that deployment is carried out smoothly and efficiently.
    • Ensure that all software releases meet the defined quality standards before deployment.
  • Stakeholder Communication:
    • Serve as the primary point of contact for all project-related communications, internally across teams and externally with stakeholders.
    • Regularly update stakeholders on project status, risks, and milestones through reports and presentations.
  • Resource Allocation:
    • Assess and allocate necessary resources, including personnel, software, and hardware, to ensure the project is adequately supported.
    • Monitor resource utilization and make adjustments as needed to avoid bottlenecks or resource constraints.
  • Risk Management:
    • Identify potential risks and develop mitigation strategies with the subject matter experts to minimize impact on the project timeline and deliverables.
    • Regularly review and update the risk management plan to reflect changes in the project landscape.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration:
    • Work with other divisions and departments to ensure software supports the program priorities and meets all integration requirements.
    • Facilitate effective communication and collaboration between the Battlespace Awareness business line and other stakeholders to promote a unified approach to program execution.
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field.
  • Extensive project management experience, preferably in software development.
  • Demonstrable understanding of optimization, applied probability, and AI/ML technology.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making capabilities.
  • Experience with tools like JIRA, Confluence, and GitHub
  • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to manage high-pressure situations and tight deadlines.
  • Must be able to obtain and hold a U.S. security clearance.

PREFERRED QAULIFICATIONS:

  • Familiarity and experience working with materiel leadership or mission partners within Army Air & Missile Defense, USMC Ground Based Air Defense, SOCOM, DHS CBP, or allied defense organizations and working knowledge of the counter-UAS and air surveillance competitive landscape.
  • Experience working on or alongside a team developing mathematical software, such as optimization solvers, estimation engines, simulation frameworks, or applied probability models.


We request transcripts as part of the early application process to understand your academic background and how your coursework supports the skills deemed critical for the role. Transcripts help us assess your technical and analytical abilities, complementing our interview process in which we also evaluate practical experience and cultural fit. If you choose not to share your transcripts, you will need to provide detailed information regarding your academic performance in relevant courses, including projects and coursework specifics, to ensure we evaluate your academic accomplishments properly. If you do provide academic transcripts, feel free to redact non-technical information (e.g., student ID, dates, non-technical coursework, etc.). Unofficial transcripts obtained online acceptable for this assessment.

$167,000—$222,000 USD

Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

 

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

  • No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

  • Please always verify communications:
    • Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
    • Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com. 

  • Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

  • What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

title: Senior Manager, Sanctions Regulatory Analysis
description:
About Airwallex

Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full.

 

Role Overview

Airwallex is seeking highly skilled Sanctions Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) to join our second line of defense (2LoD) Financial Crime Compliance (FCC) team. To support our global operations and ensure nuanced, localized oversight, we are looking for dedicated, in-region sanctions specialists across EMEA/UK.

In this role, you will act as the ultimate regional escalation point for L3 sanctions alerts to advise on complicated sanctions matches, drive sanctions investigations and efficacy of sanctions screening, determine potential reporting obligations, and assist in scaling a global sanctions program. This role requires a strategic thinker who can seamlessly translate complex regional regulatory changes into practical, scalable control enhancements across the business and multiple geographies.

Responsibilities

  • Act as an in-region Sanctions Subject Matter Expert (SME) and serve as the second-line escalation point for highly complex, ambiguous sanctions matches, special investigations, and potential block-and-reject.

  • Own L3 Sanctions case investigation and decisioning regionally, assessing applicable reporting, disclosure, and recordkeeping obligations.

  • Provide practical, timely, and risk-based sanctions advice on complex cross-border payment flows, indirect exposure, jurisdictional conflicts, new products and services, customer segments, commercial transactions, and geographic expansion.

  • Own and maintain regional Sanctions operational procedures and provide effective second-line oversight of sanctions controls implemented by first-line teams, ensuring alignment with the Global Sanctions Policy while incorporating applicable local requirements.

  • Liaise with global teams to provide actionable feedback on product-specific controls and screening technologies, leveraging in-region expertise and historical L3 escalations to ensure continuous optimization and alignment with the organization’s risk appetite.

  • Monitor US, regional, and international sanctions and export-control developments, geopolitical events, and regulatory expectations, assessing their impact on customers, products, jurisdictions, lists, systems, procedures, and risk appetite.

  • Develop and deliver targeted training and ongoing guidance for L2 sanctions reviewers, KYC, Operations, and other stakeholders on sanctions risk, alert adjudication, investigative research, discounting criteria, escalation standards, and documentation requirements.

  • Lead responses to banking partners and other external stakeholders on sanctions-related inquiries and due diligence reviews.

Qualifications

  • 7-10 years of relevant experience, preferably at a fintech, payments company, or large financial institution specializing in sanctions.

  • Experience managing sanctions alerts at the L3 level, recommending blocking/freezing transactions, assessing sanctions-related licenses and respective transactional permissibility, and managing reporting.

  • History of assessing current sanctions frameworks and recommending enhancements to strengthen the program, including designing and scaling sanctions programs.

Job summary

As a Principal Transformation Consultant, you will be responsible for managing key client relationships, ensuring the successful delivery of consulting engagements, and driving business growth. You will act as a strategic partner to senior client stakeholders, helping them navigate complex transformation initiatives, including large-scale cloud migrations and technology modernisation programmes, while expanding the firm’s footprint within the accounts you manage.

A core aspect of the role is consultative-led selling: identifying client needs through deep discovery, shaping compelling value propositions, and converting those into tangible engagements. Client partnership & engagement delivery

  • Co-develop transformation offerings in collaboration with internal practices (e.g. AI, Cloud, ITSM, Agile at Scale).

    • Team Collaboration & Knowledge Sharing

  • Act as a mentor and sparring partner for consultants at all levels, contributing to knowledge growth, capability development, and team performance.
  • Share market intelligence, client insights, and delivery learnings internally to enhance offering development and delivery practices.

    • Do you have what it takes to be a Transformation Principal?

    Essential Experience & Skills

  • A minimum of 10 years’ experience in consulting, professional services, or transformation delivery roles, with significant exposure to business and IT transformation programmes.
